chapters.summary: Staff calls the meeting to order, asks attendees to silence electronic devices, avoid the dais, and directs questions to the Sergeant at Arms. The chair is told the subcommittee is ready to begin.
chapters.title: Council staff opens Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises meeting

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Quiet, please.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to the subcommittee on zoning and franchises.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, please stand on all electronic devices.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Also, please do not approach the dais.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: If you have any questions, please ask your hand and one of us at Sergeant at Arms will kindly assist you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, we're ready to begin.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis welcomes attendees, identifies herself as chair, and notes Councilmembers Encarnacion, Sanchez, Carr, and Felder are present. She states three proposals are scheduled for votes and two public hearings.
chapters.title: Chair Farah Louis opens meeting and announces attendance

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to a meeting of the Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I am Councilmember Farrah Lewis, Chair of the Subcommittee.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This morning we are joined by Councilmembers Encarnacion, Jay Sanchez, Minority Leader Carr, and Councilmember Felder.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Today we are scheduled to vote on three proposals.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Stay in that ease.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis says votes on the sidewalk cafe application for Tero de Esquina, 158-06 Northern Boulevard, and 21-31 46th Avenue are laid over until tomorrow. She proceeds with public hearings on 1455 Coney Island Avenue and 135-27 Sapphire Street.
chapters.title: Chair Louis lays over three votes and outlines hearings

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Today we are scheduled to vote on three proposals and hold two public hearings.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: However, the following votes are laid over until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The Sidewalk Cafe application for Tero de Esquina, NYC Corp.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Formerly doing business as Cali Tejadas Bakery and Restaurant and Councilmember Thomas Henry's District.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: 158-06 Northern Boulevard Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning and Councilmember Ung's District.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: 21-3146Th Avenue Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning and Councilmember Wan's District.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We will proceed with the scheduled public hearings on the following proposals.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: 1455 Coney Island Avenue, Community Facility Rezoning and Councilmember Felder's District, 135-27 Sapphire Street and a Residential Rezoning and Councilmember Areola's District.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Please note that yesterday we held a public hearing.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: as scheduled relating to the Sidewalk Cafe application filed by Tero de Esquina, NYC Corp, and Councilmember Thomas Henry's district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This application was also noticed today for a hearing, so if there are any members of the public who would like to testify today about the Sidewalk Cafe application, please fill out a speaker's card and notify one of the sergeant at arms.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis details how to testify in person or via Zoom, the two-minute limit, written testimony submission, and decorum rules. She notes no video recording from the witness table and that public may not present audio or video recordings as testimony.
chapters.title: Chair Louis explains hybrid testimony procedures and decorum

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you are online and would like to testify about the Sidewalk Cafe application, please use the raise hand function and a team member from the subcommittee will respond and I will now go over today's meeting procedures.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This meeting is being held in hybrid format.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public who wish to testify may testify in person or via Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public wishing to testify remotely may register by visiting the New York City Council website at www.council.nyc.gov backslash land use.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: To sign up or for those of you here in person, please see one of the sergeant at arms to prepare a speaker card.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public may also view a live stream broadcast of this meeting at the council's website.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: When you are called to testify before the subcommittee, if you are joining us remotely, you will remain muted until recognized by myself to speak.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: When you are recognized, your microphone will be unmuted.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We will limit public testimony to two minutes per witness.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you have additional testimony that you would like the subcommittee to consider, or if you have written testimony that you would like to submit instead of appearing in person, please email it to landuse.com.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Testimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Written testimony may be submitted up to three days after the hearing is closed.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Please indicate the LU number and or project name in the subject line of your email.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We request that witnesses joining us remotely remain in the meeting until excused by the chair, as council members may have questions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Lastly, for everyone attending today's meeting, this is a government proceeding and decorum must be observed at all times.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public are asked not to speak during the meeting unless you are testifying.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The witness table is reserved for people who are called to testify and no video recording or photography is allowed from the witness table.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Further, members of the public may not present audio or video recordings as testimony, but you may submit transcripts of such recordings to the Sergeant at Arms for inclusion into the hearing record.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis opens the public hearing on pre-considered LUs for 1455 Coney Island Avenue, a community facility rezoning in Midwood, Brooklyn. She describes the applicant's plan for a long-term care facility for seniors and gives testimony instructions.
chapters.title: Chair Louis opens first public hearing on 1455 Coney Island Avenue

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We will now move on to the hearings that are scheduled for today, beginning with the public hearing on pre-considered LUs regarding 1455 Coney Island Avenue, a community facility rezoning proposal in Midwood, Brooklyn, and Councilmember Felder's District.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The applicant is seeking to develop a long-term care facility for seniors.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For anyone wishing to testify regarding this proposal remotely, if you have not already done so, you must register online by visiting the council's website at council.nyc.gov backslash land use.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For anyone with us in person.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Please see one of the sergeant at arms to submit a speaker card.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you prefer to submit written testimony, you can also do so by emailing it to

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Daniel's testimony at council.nyc.gov.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis notes Councilmember Felder has no remarks, calls Eric Palatnik and Anthony Hadjiouanou to testify, and has counsel administer the oath. She instructs them to restate their names and limits testimony to 10 minutes.
chapters.title: Chair Louis calls applicant panel and administers oath

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Stand at ease.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember Felder does not have remarks, so we're going to move on.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now call the applicant panel for this proposal, which consists of Eric Palatnik and Anthony Hatz.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Is Anthony here?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Well, he...

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Come on down, Anthony.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Let's go.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And Anthony, you're going to state your name because I cannot pronounce your last name.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I apologize.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Counsel, can you please administer the oath?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Anthony, how do you want to?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Could you please raise your right hand and state your name for the record?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Eric Palatnik.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Anthony, how do you want to?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Could you say that again just for our benefit?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Anthony Hadjiouanou.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Now we know how to say your name.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Do you swear to tell the truth and nothing but the truth in your testimony this morning in response to council member questions?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may begin your testimony, which is limited to 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: At eight minutes, you should start wrapping up.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: When you begin your presentation, please restate your name and the name of your organization.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Eric Palatnik introduces the long-term care facility at 1455 Coney Island Avenue, proposing rezoning from R5/C2-3 to C4-5D. He describes the site's history as a demolished long-term care facility and vacant lot, and notes the city's Coney Island Avenue study.
chapters.title: Eric Palatnik presents 1455 Coney Island Avenue rezoning overview

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Good morning, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Thank you very much for making the time to chair this committee, and good morning to everybody else that's here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: We thank you very much, and good morning to Council Member Felder, and Happy New Year to anybody who celebrated for the past week.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: We're here today on behalf of a long-term care facility located at 1455 Coney Island Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: You can see it up on the screen there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: It's a rezoning proposed from an R5 to a C2-3, from an R5 slash C2-3 to a C4-5D.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The rezoning would facilitate the creation of a long-term care facility at the property, which has historically been utilized as a long-term care facility, which was demolished.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: a few years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: That was in a previously repurposed bowling alley that was then turned into a long-term care facility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: That structure was demolished about five years ago and the lot has been vacant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Since then, we have been pursuing this rezoning, which just happens to coincide with the city's recent announcement of a study of Coney Island Avenue, which is long overdue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And it would seek to rezone the property, as I said, from an R5 to a C45D.

chapters.summary: Palatnik presents a nine-story, 95-foot, 157,000-square-foot facility with 300 beds (240 skilled nursing, 60 assisted living) and 28 parking spaces. He says Councilmember Felder requested more parking and design changes, and Community Board 14 supports the application.
chapters.title: Palatnik details building program and community board support

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: If you can go to the next slide, please, whoever's controlling the screen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: This slide on the right-hand side shows you what we are seeking to do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: If it were to be approved, you can see on the right-hand side, it would facilitate a nine-story, 95-foot-tall long-term care facility designed by Anthony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: It would be 157,000 square feet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: It would have 5.56 FAR.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: It would have 300 beds, 240 which would be skilled nursing beds, and 60 assisted living beds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: There would be 28 parking spaces.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I should note that when we originally prepared the application, we presented it to Council Member Felder, and he was

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: very concerned about the number of parking spaces, which we increased at his suggestion, as well as a few other design changes that he put into the proposal that are here today in front of you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I should also note we've met with Community Planning Board 14, who has supported the application.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

chapters.summary: Palatnik shows the existing and proposed zoning maps, noting adjacent R7A and C4-2 districts. He argues the proposed R7-equivalent density is consistent with nearby larger medical buildings and built character.
chapters.title: Palatnik explains zoning map change and surrounding context

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The next slide shows you the zoning map change, which is the essence of what we're here for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Obviously, you can see on the zoning map on both of them, the left side is existing, the right side is proposed, adjacent to the property, the top right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: is an R7A district.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: It's analogous to what we're proposing here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I should also note that the CA2 district that rests below us on Coney Island Avenue allows for buildings taller and larger than what we are proposing here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And in fact, most people in the neighborhood will

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: be familiar with the medical building that was built at Avenue L and Coney Island Avenue that is substantially larger than what we are even seeking here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: So the CA2 allows for very tall buildings and what we're seeking is consistent with the built character of what's around us.

chapters.summary: Palatnik describes the vacant site, neighboring residential building with ground-floor commercial, and proposed building layout. He notes first-floor lobby and amenity space, cellar parking, and upper-floor care facility.
chapters.title: Palatnik reviews site context and building elevations

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Next slide just sort of shows you everything I've already spoken about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: If you can go one more slide forward please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The next slide, slide five, just gives you a good view of the context of the neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The site itself is now vacant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: There are no cars or trucks being parked on it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: You can see to the left of us is an existing residential building with ground floor commercial, and that extends pretty much entirely up the block to the left of us on Avenue K.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: We are simply a continuation of that larger density on our site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And I could point to, if you can go to plan sheet seven, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Page 7 shows you what the building will look like from an elevation perspective.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: You could see that the first floor will be a lobby and amenity space.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The cellar and the sub-cellar will be parking and accessory space.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And then the long-term care facility is located up top.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I'll pause on the next slide and stop the conversation because I think I've given you enough information for you to act on things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: But if you'd like more, I'd be happy to continue on.

chapters.summary: Palatnik points to a 148-foot medical building allowed as-of-right in the adjacent C4-2 district. He argues the proposed rezoning is smaller than what existing zoning permits and similar to surrounding R7A context.
chapters.title: Palatnik compares proposal to taller as-of-right medical building

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The next slide is relevant because I mentioned a few moments ago the taller medical bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, slide eight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I apologize.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Where you were a second ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: This slide is relevant because you can see the building on the right-hand side at 148 feet tall.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: That's the medical building that's allowed to be constructed as of right in the CA2 district that shares the block with us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The point that I'm simply trying to raise through this discussion is our rezoning, which is seeking to go to an R7 equivalent, is really similar to what's around us as far as existing R7 zoning, and it's even smaller than what the CA2 allows for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: That concludes my presentation.

chapters.summary: Palatnik shows renderings of the proposed building, highlighting an atrium, landscaped rooftop terrace, chapel, recreation, and exercise spaces. He says the design aims to feel like a home rather than an institution.
chapters.title: Palatnik presents renderings and amenities for long-term care facility

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I guess I'll ask whoever's controlling the screen, if you could just click forward to the plans, the proposed plans, which is after page 15.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And you can stop on the rendering at the front so everybody can see how beautiful the building is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: There you go.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And the building is really proposed to be a stunning building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I dare say one of the nicest buildings that I've seen a rendering for on Coney Island Avenue in quite some time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The middle part of it that you're looking at is a proposed atrium area where there'll be a common area for building residents so they could be exposed to sunlight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: They should catch great westerly sunsets and things like that, let lights in, let light in, make them feel like they're living somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: That's part of their home where they are now and not coming into an institution of any sort.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And the rooftop on the top right is beautifully well landscaped with an

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: outdoor terrace area, again, for people to have space to be outside.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And the building is filled with all sorts of other different amenities, including a chapel, including common space, including space for recreation, space for working out, all to give people the chance to not only live in this building as an assisted living building, but also have it feel like a home.

chapters.summary: Palatnik says the project was proposed by a not-for-profit but a contract dispute arose with the owner, Centers Healthcare. He hopes the not-for-profit can be restored as operator, but if not, Centers Healthcare will develop the long-term care facility itself.
chapters.title: Palatnik addresses not-for-profit dispute and fallback operator

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And I'll mention the final note is the building is being proposed by a not-for-profit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The not-for-profit has been the one pursuing the application along with ownership of the property.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: There has been a bit of a dispute between the two in the last few weeks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Maybe some people on the committee may have heard about that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: They are working to resolve it so that the not-for-profit can continue on and operate, continue on, build and operate the premises.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And should that not happen, which everybody is working towards, and we're hoping we'll use the full ULURP timeframe to let them achieve that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: If that should not be the case, then the owner of the property currently

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: will develop the property as a long-term care facility themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: But we are desperately trying to save the relationship with the not-for-profit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And I want to thank the council member who has been involved in discussions with everybody in the midst of his holiday, as well as everybody else who's been involved to do so.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And we're hoping that we'll have a resolution to report to you at some point in the future before this is over.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your time.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks what assurances exist that the development will be a nursing home and nonprofit. Palatnik says state-allocated beds require long-term care use, and if the Sephardic Nursing Home does not operate it, Centers Healthcare will.
chapters.title: Chair Louis questions assurances on nursing home and nonprofit operation

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions before I hand it over to Councilman Felder.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: It is the subcommittee's understanding that this project was initially proposed at

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: as a nursing home, but the operator with whom the applicant was going to partner with, as you just mentioned, is no longer taking part of the project.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: What assurances can you provide that this proposed development will in fact be a nursing home and a nonprofit?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I can make...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Quite a bit of assurance is that it will be developed as a long-term care facility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The reason for that is for a couple of different reasons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: First of all, the beds have already been allocated by the state for that purpose, and beds are very difficult to get approval for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Second, the landowner is also one of the largest assisted living facility providers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: In the metropolitan area, specifically in New York City, and is New York City-based.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The name of their company is Centers Healthcare, and they're very well recognized and respected for their work in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: So if it is not operated by the Sephardic Nursing Home, which is the not-for-profit that was in contract,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: with them, then it will be operated by Centers Healthcare.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Either way, it will be operated as a long-term care facility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The bigger question that's, I think, germane, not so much from a land use perspective, but from an emotional and personal perspective for many people, is that the proposal right now, up until now, has been for Sephardic Nursing Home, which is a not-for-profit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: To be operating it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Obviously, a not-for-profit comes from an altruistic motive, whereas Centers Healthcare is a for-profit organization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Nothing wrong with being for-profit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: We all live in New York City, and it's okay to be for-profit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: But we all believe in our heart of hearts that the not-for-profit is a better fit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And I'm not involved in those negotiations, and neither is the council member.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: But everybody, such as the council member and myself, have been working with those two parties to try to get them to an agreement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And a phone call I received last night was that they're continuing to work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And I understand we have until November 11th before the EULA process times out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And we're hoping that we could use that time before the council acts on its entirety to report back to you before a vote is taken that the wishes of the community and that we presented earlier are a dear deal.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks how many jobs the project will create. Palatnik estimates 100-150 construction workers and says operational hiring will include local lower-level positions, with senior management from other facilities.
chapters.title: Chair Louis asks about construction and operational jobs

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I can't give you exact numbers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Probably somewhere in the neighborhood of 100 to 150 people would be working on the building to construct the building, including laborers, engineers, builders, concrete, steel workers, glaziers, all those kinds of trades would be working.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And they will be using local labor to construct the building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: As far as operating the building goes, senior level management staff is going to be coming from other facilities because that's how most businesses operate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And then they will be hiring new people for some of the lower level positions to give them the chance to come in and join the organization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The way the organization works is they give people from within the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: to rise within the organization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: So if there are people that are working in other facilities that started at a lower job status, then now they'll be given an opportunity to move into a managerial position and the new people will be given the chance to come and take their place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: There'll also be transportation provided to people to and from the facility, both employees as well as

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: residents and their family members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: The idea will be that people will be living there, will be coming from the community, their family members will be from the community, so there will be a shuttle bus that will be operating in the area that people will be able to summons to get people to and from.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: It won't be operating as routinely as a city bus, but it will be available.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks which trades will be involved. Palatnik lists glaziers, electricians, mechanical engineering, duct work, and other building trades.
chapters.title: Chair Louis asks which trades will be used

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: So you mentioned trades.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Which trades and...

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Do you have an idea yet which trade?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I just meant glaziers and electricians and mechanical engineering and duct work and all the building trades is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks how the proposed height relates to surrounding buildings. Palatnik compares the 95-foot building to nearby 66-75 foot buildings and a taller C8 building, arguing it is contextual.
chapters.title: Chair Louis questions building height relative to surrounding homes

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Can you please go over again how the height of the proposed building relates to surrounding homes and businesses?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Yeah, that's up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: If we can go back to the picture that I showed a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Which page?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I'll get to the page to tell the person controlling the screen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I think it was page eight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: So this picture is helpful because it shows you the heights of surrounding buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Coney Island Avenue is not necessarily the avenue that you've seen any development on in my lifetime, in fact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I don't believe I've seen much developed in my lifetime.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I think I can count the number of buildings and new buildings, specifically residential, that have been built in this part of Coney Island in one hand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: So you don't see much taller buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: That's what...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: But you can see on the side streets some of the proliferation that has occurred through the years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: For example, on Avenue M, you can see over there at the top of the page a whole host of larger, taller, newer buildings which have been constructed that are 75 feet tall, 71 feet tall, 66 feet tall.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: We're at 95 feet tall.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: So we're somewhat consistent with those, but even more so consistent with the building immediately across the street from us in the C8 zone, which was just built as well, which I would dare say is too tall for the neighborhood and overwhelms the community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: I don't think many people in the area are a fan of its height, but it towers even over the property by 50 feet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: And as I mentioned a moment ago, Avenue K is zoned R7A, which is analogous to what we're requesting here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: So although those buildings that are in R7A are older buildings, which look mostly like they're pre-war buildings built in the 30s, 40s, or maybe some post-war.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: definitely 50, 60, 70, 80 years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: So none of those buildings have any affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: All of them are older buildings working with old electrical and mechanical systems and don't have any of the modern amenities that most people would want.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: Ceiling heights are low, things like that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Palatnik
utterances.text: So I think the building that we're requesting is a good example of a modern contextual building, albeit a little bit higher than what's on the side streets.

chapters.summary: Richard Lobel introduces the rezoning from R4 to R6A, proposing a six-story plus cellar building with about 186,000 square feet and 268 dwelling units. He notes MIH option one and support from Queens Community Board 10, the Borough President, and City Planning.
chapters.title: Richard Lobel presents 135-27 Sapphire Street rezoning rationale

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Lewis, Council Members, Richard Lobel of Sheldon Lobel PC, joined by the applicant team and proud to bring 13527 Sapphire Street rezoning application to the subcommittee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And we hope that the council will join in the overwhelming support of Queens Community Board 10 in the vote of 29 to 1 in favor, as well as the Queensborough President and City Planning in supporting this application.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I will give a brief discussion with regards to the land use rationale of this application.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Dan Ruzzo will then talk about the architectural aspects, and then the entire applicant team is happy to answer questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So why are we here today?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: This is a rezoning from an existing R4 district to an R6A district.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Rezoning would allow for the building of a new six-story plus cellar residential building, a total floor area of roughly 186,000 square feet and roughly 268 dwelling units.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: This, of course, would be accompanied by a text amendment application for MIH, mandatory inclusionary housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The app concurrently has penciled this out at option one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The next slide is the proposed development in terms of the numbers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: This building, again, six stories plus cellar at 186,000 square feet, a base height of five stories and a total height of 65 feet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Parking would be 118 spaces in the cellar, which Dan can discuss.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: 268 units with the breakdown of studios ones and twos, as you can see before you, and roughly 67 units at option one.

utterances.text: The next slide is a zoning map.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Which I think tells part of the story in terms of why this is a meritorious rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: It's that little dotted area to the right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So there's already a context on this block for increased zoning density.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So the remainder of the block after this rezoning would be R6A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel
utterances.text: There was also the Linden Boulevard rezoning two blocks to the west of us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.text: Hello, committee.

utterances.text: Thank you for your time today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: As Richard has just said, the proposal here shows a six-story building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: It is a five-story mass with a six-floor that sets back in order to minimize the height of the building and provide a more contextual envelope to the surrounding homes around us, which

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: The Lindenwood Diner, which is just to the right of the red.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: The red square that you see right there along Linden Boulevard has been replaced, and that has been replaced still under construction with 12- and 14-story buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: So we would be smaller, but we are trying to still be sensitive toward the rest of the scale that's surrounding us in the neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: To that end, the proposal here, as Richard has said, is for 268 units, 67 of which would be affordable.

utterances.text: And the grade actually lowers as you go along the right and you go down.

utterances.text: The proposal here shows a bidirectional driveway on the left-hand side of the screen that provides access to both 79th and to Sapphire as well as entrance into our proposed parking garage,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: which is completely above grade along Sapphire on the bottom of the screen.

chapters.summary: Ruzzo explains the first-floor lobby and terrace, stepped massing up to the fifth floor, and a sixth-floor setback around the perimeter. He notes voluntary setbacks from the sidewalk to create a natural buffer and absorb stormwater.
chapters.title: Ruzzo details floor setbacks and green buffer

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: The first level and lobby entrance is primarily housing with a large terrace that occurs on the inside.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: The building continues to grow and step up to the fifth floor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: And then we have a setback that occurs around the entire perimeter at the sixth floor, again, minimizing the height and feel of the building from street level.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: You'll also note the green that surrounds the entire property.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: We elected to push back the building from the sidewalk line voluntarily to create a natural buffer that both provides for a softer streetscape as well as greenery that would absorb water and stormwater in any type of a flooding situation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: So we felt it was a benefit for both the residents of the community and for the residents of the building.

chapters.summary: Ruzzo shows a section and explains a proposed DOT grade change of 2 to 10 feet. He says the driveway design allows parking access to continue and the building to remain in service during street raising.
chapters.title: Ruzzo addresses DOT grade change and future-proofed driveway

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Here we'll see in section the building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Again, the gray representing the driveway and the parking garage below.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: There is a proposed DOT grade change for this entire area and this entire street system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: To that end, because of the way the building is designed and situated with respect to the current grade,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: should DOT raise the grade around the perimeter, which is going to be a pretty meaningful raise of roughly 2 feet to 10 feet across, the way our driveway is designed, it allows for the building to not be taken out of service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: The parking would actually still be able to be accessed, and we would have access to effectively one street, their 79th or Sapphire, as DOT proposes and does that work.

chapters.summary: Ruzzo shows renderings of the building in context, including the setback and greenscape. He describes a gabion wall system for the parking level that allows water and air movement, and a knockout panel for future DOT grade changes.
chapters.title: Ruzzo presents renderings and gabion wall flood design

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: I think the renderings will show a little bit better.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: So here we can see the building within context.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: The Lindenwood Diner development is the red and dark brown, blackish charcoal building that you're seeing to our right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: We're the white building right in the center of the screen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: As you can see, we are set back from the street, and we propose quite a bit of greenscape all around.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: This is our corner and lobby entrance on 79th Street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: As you can see, the grade slightly dips as we go all the way around the building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: And you'll note that that sixth floor feels a little bit more de minimis from the street because it's set back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Here you're seeing the driveway entrance along Sapphire, and you'll see that big blank wall right above it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Sapphire would be raised by as much as 10 feet, so essentially the new grade one day would be at relatively the height of the top of the door right now, the garage door that you can see on the left.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: So what that allows us to do is we'll have a knockout panel planned into the building as it's constructed, and when DOT raises the streets, we'll just raise the door into a panel that's already designed to be removed so that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: the building is designed to be future-proofed for DOT to be able to do its work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: What you're seeing on the ground floor there is a gabion wall system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: That is actually walls that are used in highway design.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: It's basically chicken wire or steel wire with boulders inside of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: It creates a fully permeable envelope that allows water to freely move into and out of the building because we are in a flood zone, as well as providing for a very natural environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Air can also come in and out, and that is a parking level, so it's always nice to be able to have some breeze and be able to breathe in there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: When the grade is raised, we would simply pour a concrete wall, a foundation wall, behind the gabion wall system, and then that creates our bathtub, if you will, or our sealed cellar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: All of this can be done, as I said, without taking the building out of service at all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Daniel Ruzzo
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.text: I think that's it.

utterances.text: I really want to thank Mr.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: that were suggested.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: As you can see, this is a...

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: forward-thinking project.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: It brings in resiliency.

utterances.text: It just brings in affordability, and we're looking forward to this.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: And I think that when you look at this building and you see the kind of interaction that this particular group has had with the community and the

utterances.text: kind of consideration that they gave the community, it really should be a best practice for all developers, and they'd get a lot less pushback when it came to development within their communities.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: Thank you again to the team.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: Thank you to the Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises for hearing this project, and it does have my full support.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: And thank you, Chair.

chapters.title: Chair Louis asks about Jewel Streets plan consistency

utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.text: I have a couple of quick questions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Is the applicant team aware of the Jewel Streets neighborhood?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake
utterances.text: Danielle Drake with H2M Architects and Engineers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake
utterances.text: So we've been very knowledgeable of the Jewel Streets plans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake
utterances.text: We've discussed with various members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake
utterances.text: We have built the project to align with the Jewel Streets plan so that the road raising, which is the major implementation in this area that they're looking to do to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake

utterances.text: Can you discuss some more the sewer infrastructure in the area, how this large project will connect with the sewer?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I'm very familiar with the area, so I think you guys did an excellent job covering the fact that it's in a flood zone.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: But if you could talk about the sewer infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake
utterances.text: So the sewer infrastructure there now, we have done preliminary analyses that we've submitted to DEP.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake
utterances.text: And we've been able to ascertain that the existing infrastructure within the roadway can support this building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake
utterances.text: It will require a sewer extension along 149th.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake
utterances.text: Just to get

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake
utterances.text: physically to the building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake
utterances.text: But other than that, the actual sewer infrastructure within the roadway is able to support it, as well as the drainage infrastructure within the roadway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Danielle Drake

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis

summary: The Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises held public hearings on two pre-considered land use applications: a long-term care facility at 1455 Coney Island Avenue in Brooklyn and a residential rezoning at 135-27 Sapphire Street in Queens.
Applicants presented project details and answered questions from Chair Farah Louis and Council Member Simcha Felder; no members of the public testified on either proposal.
Both public hearings were closed and the items were laid over; the sidewalk cafe application for Tero de Esquina remained closed with no speakers, and the meeting was adjourned.
